title: Quasi-coherence of exterior sheaves on affine schemes
statement: Let X be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], M a quasi-coherent O_X-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, pqf-def-coherent], and n a natural number. Then exteriorSheaf M n, the sheafification of the sectionwise nth exterior powers [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power], is quasi-coherent. No finiteness or local-freeness assumption is made.

proof.text: Put A=Gamma(X,top) and P=Gamma(X,M). The affine tilde-Gamma equivalence identifies M with the associated A-module P. Its sections on each principal open D(f) are P_f. This uses only quasi-coherence and affinity, not finite presentation or local freeness.

Follow Stacks Lemma 26.7.2(2): localization of an exterior power is the exterior power of the localized module. Construct the forward alternating map by sending a tuple of fractions to the wedge of its numerators divided by the product of its denominators. The alternating universal property gives the inverse after localization. Both composites agree with the identity on pure wedges, which generate. These maps commute with restriction between principal opens because their values on each pure wedge agree. Thus on the principal-open basis the exterior presheaf of M is the associated module of the algebraic exterior power of P. Sheafification identifies exteriorSheaf M n with this associated module. Associated modules are quasi-coherent, and quasi-coherence is invariant under isomorphism. This includes degree zero, zero modules, arbitrary characteristic, and the zero ring/empty scheme.
